type: CAPABILITY BUILT (the r44-named bottleneck) + CONTROL REPAIR
title: I built the fix I named last round. The system can now answer with a list, a string, a hash, an integer -- and zero. That removes the answer-type bottleneck. It does not change what the system knows.

what_r44_named_and_r45_built.the_bottleneck: r44 measured that all 23 verbs returned exactly 'the number of non-empty lines the program printed', 23 of 23. 'sha256 of <f>' answered 1. 'first column of <f>' answered 7. Zero was unrepresentable.
what_r44_named_and_r45_built.the_fix: postcondition kinds whose answer has a TYPE: stdout_lines (list), stdout_text (verbatim str), stdout_first_token (the hash), stdout_integer_value (THE INTEGER PRINTED, e.g. wc -l -> 4), stdout_line_count_or_zero (a count where 0 is sayable).

measured_after.'count the lines of' an EMPTY file: 0 (was: 1, and it reported that as VERIFIED)

what_r44_named_and_r45_built.left_alone_deliberately: stdout_line_count still fails closed on zero. It is load-bearing for the ownership gate (see below), so the count-with-zero lives in a SEPARATE kind rather than loosening the old one.

the_control_repair.the_flaw: causal_ablation_pass was computed as `not verify_postcondition(post, execution_result={})`. That infers 'the goal did not already hold' from an EMPTY generic check rather than from the held-out world. It works only while every postcondition kind happens to fail on an empty world -- which is exactly why r44's zero-fix refused EVERY skill with REQUIRED_TRUE_MISSING:causal_ablation_pass.
the_control_repair.the_fix: a new _heldout_pre_state() that OBSERVES the held-out world before anything runs: for file contracts it reads the file; for stdout contracts there is no pre-state and it says so. The ablation now asks the same question it will ask after execution.

verified_both_directions.goal already true in the pre-state: pre_ok=True -> ablation_pass=False (refuse: the skill would prove nothing)
verified_both_directions.every stdout contract: pre_ok=False -> ablation_pass=True, for all five kinds, because nothing has run

REAL: A skill can now return the lines, the text, the hash, the printed integer, and zero (measured, 12 tests).
The zero-answer hole from r44 is CLOSED for counting questions, without loosening the check the gate depends on.
The ablation control no longer depends on an unrelated check failing, so a future postcondition that can verify on an empty world will not silently break qualification.
Everything from r41-r44 still stands: 23/33 track, composition 3/4, environment shift 23/23 in three of five.
NOT_REAL: That this changed what the system KNOWS. It still learns one anchored sentence -> one argv. The answer type got richer; the understanding did not.

That 'shape is not truth' is solved. 2026 production literature is explicit: a schema is a promise about STRUCTURE, not accuracy ('the biggest killer isn't parse errors, it's schema-valid garbage'). stdout_first_token now returns a well-typed 64-char string whether or not it is the right file's hash.

That a path containing a SPACE works. NEW measured limitation: the goal language is whitespace-delimited and unquoted, so '/tmp/count the lines of_t.txt' becomes skeleton 'count the lines of ?path0 the lines ?path1' -- two parameters, fixed at two. It re-matches the identical string and cannot generalise to a differently-shaped spacey path.
That this touches a public benchmark: still ZERO public-benchmark numbers.
That the reliability arithmetic moved: 318 steps at 99% per step is still 4.09%.

the_sentience_claim: Unchanged. A typed result is still a result: a list of strings, an integer, a hash. What the system has is a durable table of anchored regexes, an argv per entry, and now a richer return type. There is no state about itself, no goal, no preference, no 'I'. Making the output better typed is a software-engineering improvement of exactly the kind that has no relationship to being a creature.

the_smartest_things_to_do_next.1: Add QUOTING to the goal language, or forbid spaces in bound parameters. The space-in-path defect is a two-parameter skeleton that can never generalise, and it is cheaper to fix now than after more skills depend on the current tokenisation.
the_smartest_things_to_do_next.2: Choose the contract kind from the GOAL, not from the caller. Today a skill's answer type is whatever postcondition it was taught with, so 'count the lines of' still answers 1 unless the teacher picks stdout_integer_value. Inferring the contract from the goal text is what would make the 23 verbs answer their own goals rather than a line count.
the_smartest_things_to_do_next.3: Add semantic validators alongside the type (range, freshness, expected-shape). The 2026 production reading is that typed contracts catch parse failures and miss semantic ones -- 'schema-valid garbage' is the dominant wrongness.
the_smartest_things_to_do_next.4: Still not writing. A typed answer makes a destructive mistake easier to describe, not less destructive.

artifacts.changed: causal_trace_to_skill_compiler_v1.py -- five new postcondition kinds, verifier dispatch, _heldout_pre_state, explicit ablation
